args.message: Hi have a look at program.md and let's kick off a new experiment!

args.description: Baseline run from the starting train.py in the autoresearch/may3-2 working tree; note train.py already had uncommitted local changes before this loop began.
args.outcome_vs_prediction: baseline: no prior hypothesis; establishes current best val_bpb at 2.073040 after 36 optimizer steps.

args.message: Committed the pre-existing train.py state as 34effa08d49de3cfac82d7fe5ede5701cf914127 so subsequent hypothesis commits isolate only new train.py changes. Baseline metric was measured from the same train.py content before this bookkeeping commit.

args.description: Reduce WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.25 so the optimizer spends more of the 30-second budget at full learning rate before decaying.
args.reasoning: In exp-001 the smoothed train loss was still decreasing cleanly through the halfway point, but the schedule began warmdown at about 50% progress and reached lrm 0.07 by the final step. With only 36 optimizer steps, decaying for half the measured budget may under-train the model.

prediction.mechanism: More full-LR updates should improve early optimization before the short run ends, while still leaving a final quarter-budget cooldown for stability.
prediction.side_effects: Slightly higher late training loss variance or possible overshoot; no meaningful memory change.

args.summary: Shortened LR warmdown from 50% to 25% of the measured training budget.

args.message: Committed chg-001 as 3a9e1fba4feedbbe39a11874b2a0e8326511ca70 with message 'Shorten LR warmdown'.

args.description: Shortened LR warmdown from 50% to 25% of the 30-second training budget.
args.outcome_vs_prediction: partially matched: val_bpb dropped by 0.004805 versus baseline 2.073040, confirming that the 50% warmdown was too conservative, but the gain landed just below the predicted 0.005-0.020 range. Mechanism still looks right because the run kept lrm=1.00 until about 75% progress and improved without extra memory.

args.description: Reduce WARMDOWN_RATIO further from 0.25 to 0.10 so LR stays at full strength until the final tenth of the short run.
args.reasoning: Exp-002 improved over exp-001 by delaying warmdown, and its loss trace stayed smooth with lrm=1.00 through roughly 75% progress. Since the measured budget only yields 36 steps and no instability appeared, the run may still benefit from more full-rate optimization before the last few cooldown steps.

prediction.mechanism: If the main bottleneck is too few high-LR updates, delaying decay until the last 10% should extract a little more fit from the same token budget.
prediction.side_effects: Higher risk of mild overshoot near the end; memory and wall-clock should remain unchanged.

args.summary: Shortened LR warmdown further from 25% to 10% of the measured training budget.

args.message: Committed chg-002 as 07e901e0bde76da4f96458df66b1f32b79540008 with message 'Delay LR warmdown further'.

args.description: Shortened LR warmdown further from 25% to 10% of the 30-second training budget.
args.outcome_vs_prediction: matched: val_bpb dropped by 0.003874 versus exp-002, within the predicted 0.001-0.008 range. The delayed-decay mechanism looks confirmed for this short-budget setup; it also allowed 37 steps instead of 36 because the run timing changed slightly, with no memory change.

args.description: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.10 to 0.0 so the 30-second run uses the full initial learning rate for every optimizer step.
args.reasoning: Exp-002 and exp-003 both improved as LR warmdown was delayed. Exp-003 still showed a smooth loss trace and improved despite decaying only in the final few steps, suggesting the short run is bottlenecked by too few high-rate updates rather than late instability.

prediction.mechanism: Removing the last cooldown should add a few more effective high-LR updates in a 36-37 step budget, improving fit if overshoot is not yet limiting.
prediction.side_effects: Risk of a small regression from no final stabilization; memory unchanged.

args.summary: Removed LR warmdown entirely for the short run.

args.message: Committed chg-003 as ddf3b9e54881478cde82de53e8d181242cfdbad7 with message 'Remove LR warmdown'.

args.description: Removed LR warmdown entirely for the 30-second training budget.
args.outcome_vs_prediction: matched: val_bpb dropped by 0.003302 versus exp-003, within the predicted 0.0005-0.004 range. The result strongly supports the mechanism that these short runs are high-LR-update limited; no final cooldown was needed for stability.

args.description: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05 while keeping no warmdown.
args.reasoning: Exp-004 improved by using full learning rate for every step, which suggests the 30-second run is still optimization-rate limited. Matrix parameters are trained by Muon and dominate transformer adaptation, so a modest 25% matrix LR increase may get more useful movement in the same 37 steps without changing memory or evaluation cost.

prediction.mechanism: Higher Muon LR should accelerate transformer matrix fitting under the very short step budget, provided it does not destabilize late updates now that warmdown is gone.
prediction.side_effects: Could overshoot and regress; train loss may be slightly noisier; memory unchanged.

args.summary: Increased Muon matrix learning rate by 25%.

args.purpose: record prototype training-budget context communicated by the user

module_summaries.summary: Defines the fixed training and evaluation setup, including the prototype TIME_BUDGET of 30 seconds.
Contains the experiment surface. Runs are judged within the fixed short budget, so changes optimize relative val_bpb under a tiny training window rather than final model quality.
Document that this checkout is using a 30-second prototype budget instead of a longer production-style training run.

hot_path_hypothesis.description: Absolute model quality is expected to be weak because each experiment trains for only 30 seconds.
hot_path_hypothesis.reasoning: The user explicitly communicated that poor-looking results are intentional for this prototype. Interpret val_bpb as a relative signal between experiments run under the same short budget, not as evidence that the final model should be good.

open_questions: Do not treat high absolute val_bpb or low sample quality as unexpected failure; the 30-second budget is intentionally too short for a good model.
Use this event as provenance that the short-budget interpretation was communicated by the user.
A longer training budget would be a separate experiment regime and should not be compared directly against this run history.
